newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber said subdued in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber said subdued in slow market.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished quietly on Tuesday with volumes said to be thin except for spot deals for RSS3 grade rubber, dealers said.

"The manufacturers are sidelined. At least, I don't see many of them around. With Tokyo coming off, people were not very keen about coming into the market because they think prices here will also go down," a dealer said.
The key September contract in Tokyo shed 1.2 yen to end at 140.8, mainly on long liquidation.
"Nobody really asked for any offers this afternoon. It's pretty quiet," one dealer said.
Market sentiment here was also slightly depressed by the Songkran Buddhist holiday in Thailand.

"It looks pretty soft today," one dealer said, adding the market activity may thin out ahead of the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holiday on Friday, which will shut down markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.

At around 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 114.75 U.S. cents a kg from 115.50 cents. August RSS1 was seen at 165.25 Singapore cents (US$1.14) a kg from 166.25 cents. January/March TSR20 was seen at 114.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.75 cents.
